newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to indict sacked minister in arms deal.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to indict sacked minister in arms deal.

text.p: Former South Korean defence minister Lee Yang-ho will be formally indicted on bribery charges on Monday, a prosecution official said.

Lee, who is already in custody, will be charged with accepting 150 million won ($181,000) as part of his share of payments made to a Korean-American arms dealer in connection with a military purchase of helicopters from Daewoo Group the official said.
Lee was sacked as Defence Minister last month hours before allegations surfaced in parliament that he indirectly took money from Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd.
Daewoo has admitted paying around 300 million won to the arms dealer, but as a commission, not a bribe.
Lee was arrested on October 26, and prosecutors said at the time he had admitted to receiving the money.
The case has embarrassed the government of President Kim Young-sam, who has staked his reputation on rooting out corruption from South Korean society.
